content: Balsalazide is a medication used to treat ulcerative colitis, a specific bowel disease. It works by reducing symptoms such as diarrhea, rectal bleeding, and abdominal pain. This drug belongs to the class of medications known as aminosalicylates. To use balsalazide, take it orally as directed by your doctor, typically three times daily. It can be taken with or without food. It is important to drink plenty of fluids during treatment unless otherwise instructed by your doctor. If you have difficulty swallowing the capsules, you may open them and sprinkle the contents onto a spoonful of applesauce. Consume the mixture immediately without chewing. For best results, use this medication regularly as prescribed. Common side effects of balsalazide include headache, nausea, vomiting, joint pain, diarrhea, abdominal pain, fever, sore throat, difficulty sleeping, and loss of appetite. While these side effects are generally mild, it is important to note that balsalazide can rarely worsen ulcerative colitis. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare but possible. If you experience any unusual or severe symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Before starting balsalazide, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, other aminosalicylates (such as mesalamine or olsalazine), salicylates (such as aspirin), or sulfasalazine. Additionally, disclose any other allergies or medical conditions you may have. This medication may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Balsalazide may increase your sensitivity to sunlight, especially if you have pre-existing skin conditions like eczema or atopic dermatitis. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. This medication also contains sodium and is chemically similar to aspirin. Children and teenagers under 18 should not take aspirin if they have chickenpox, the flu, or an undiagnosed illness, or if they have recently received a vaccine. During pregnancy, balsalazide should only be used when clearly needed. It may pass into breast milk, so consult your doctor about the risks and benefits if you are breastfeeding. There is limited clinical data on its effects during lactation, so the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother’s need for the medication and any potential risks to the infant. Drug interactions may alter how balsalazide works or increase the risk of serious side effects. Inform your doctor and pharmacist about all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements. Balsalazide is very similar to mesalamine, so avoid using both medications simultaneously unless directed by your doctor. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, such as urine normetanephrine levels, potentially causing false results. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store balsalazide at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication as instructed by your pharmacist or local waste disposal company. Before starting therapy, your doctor may evaluate your kidney function. During treatment, regular medical and lab tests, such as kidney and liver function tests, may be necessary to monitor your progress and detect any potential side effects. Always follow your doctor’s instructions and attend all scheduled medical appointments. In case of an overdose, seek immediate medical attention. If someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about balsalazide. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
